full_judgment:
2. The pre-emptor opposite party No. 1 instituted Misc. Case No. 144/73 u/s. 96 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act. The learned Munsif found that the Misc. case was not time-barred and that the per-emptors had locus standi to preempt the case land but dismissed the Misc. Case on the ground that the case land was reconvened to the vendor-petitioner in pursuance of a contemporaneous agreement for reconveyance. On appeal, the learned Subordinate Judge, Noakhali by his judgment and Order date. 26.7.79 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 203/76 allowed the same and also allowed the Misc. case on the ground that as the agreement for reconveyance was found to be false the reconveyance was of no legal effect. 

 6. Section 96(12) of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act provides that an appeal shall lie to the ordinary Civil Appellate Court from any order of a court under this section. The ordinary Civil Appellate Court is the Court of the District Judge when the pre-emotion case is tried by a Munsif. The District Judge transfers the appeal to any Subordinate Judge under his administrative control u/s. 22 of the Civil Courts Act, 1987. Hence Judgment and Order passed by the Subordinate Judge on appeal u/s. 96 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act is a Judgment and Order passed by the District Judge himself. The District Judge cannot entertain a revisional application u/s. 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure against his own judgment and order.
